title: ICA Lens: Non-Gaussianity Reveals Interpretable Directions in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2606.11722v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Finding human-interpretable directions in language-model activations is important for understanding and controlling model behavior. These directions are usually discovered through indirect learning objectives such as sparse reconstruction, but it remains unclear what existing statistical structure distinguishes interpretable directions and whether that structure can be used directly for feature discovery. We find that non-Gaussianity provides such a signature: projection distributions of natural-text residual-stream activations along sparse autoencoder (SAE) decoder directions are substantially more non-Gaussian than those along random directions, with most contexts forming a concentrated background and recurring patterns often occupying one tail. This raises a natural question: if interpretable directions tend to have non-Gaussian projection distributions, can we discover them by searching for non-Gaussian directions directly

translated_title: ICA Lens：非高斯性揭示语言模型中的可解释方向
translated_abstract: 在语言模型激活中寻找人类可解释的方向，对于理解和控制模型行为至关重要。这些方向通常通过间接的学习目标（如稀疏重建）来发现，但目前尚不清楚是何种统计结构区分了可解释方向，以及这种结构能否直接用于特征发现。我们发现非高斯性提供了这样一种特征标志：自然文本残差流激活沿稀疏自编码器（SAE）解码器方向的投影分布，明显比沿随机方向的投影分布更加非高斯，其中大多数上下文形成一个集中的背景，而重复出现的模式往往占据分布的一个尾部。这引出了一个自然的问题：如果可解释方向往往具有非高斯的投影分布，我们能否通过直接搜索非高斯方向来发现它们？
tldr: 该论文发现语言模型激活中可解释方向具有非高斯投影分布这一统计特征，并提出可以通过直接搜索非高斯方向来发现可解释特征，而无需依赖稀疏重建等间接学习目标。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that interpretable directions in language model activations exhibit non-Gaussian projection distributions, and proposes discovering interpretable features by directly searching for non-Gaussian directions instead of relying on indirect learning objectives such as sparse reconstruction.
